newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Groups seek stricter control over mahogany trade.
newsitem.headline: Groups seek stricter control over mahogany trade.

text.p: Two leading international environmental watchdogs promised on Monday to stop calling for a moratorium on mahogany logging if a world forum on endangered species allows stricter control over the trade.

Greenpeace and Friends of the Earth made the pledge ahead of this week's crucial vote by the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) on a proposal by Bolivia and the United States to list bigleaf mahogany on its Appendix II, which allows for controlled trade.
The proposal has gained support from Latin American countries at the CITES meeting ending in Harare on Friday.

"Friends of the Earth and Greenpeace today promised to stop calling for a moratorium on mahogany logging and trade if an Appendix II listing under CITES is agreed and properly implemented," the two groups said in a statement.
The groups have been calling since 1992 for a moratorium on mahogany trade until guarantees that it was coming from legal and sustainable sources were in place.
The mahogany proposal is one of about 80 on the CITES agenda, dominated by a contentious debate on a proposal by three southern African countries to relax a ban on ivory trade.
Voting on the proposals is scheduled for towards the end of the meeting.
